The Veil Days

The Veil Days

Veil Days are outside the month.
No one likes to schedule weddings on them, but everyone schedules necessary things.

Each Veil Day sits between two months. In many towns, bells ring once at dawn and once at deep night:
to mark that time “slipped” and returned.

Veil Day List

  1. Ash-Veil
    Custom: hearths are cleaned; names of the dead are spoken once.
    Omen: the past demands payment.

  2. Mirror-Veil
    Custom: no oaths; people avoid promises and “final words”.
    Omen: truth is visible, but not kind.

  3. Chain-Veil
    Custom: debts are recorded, contracts renewed, prisoners counted.
    Omen: what binds you tightens.

  4. Lantern-Veil
    Custom: lantern lines in streets; travelers move under escort.
    Omen: guidance appears — but only if you look.

  5. Knife-Veil
    Custom: tools are sharpened; militia drills; hidden weapons inspected.
    Omen: conflict chooses a direction.

  6. Suture-Veil
    Custom: healers work without charge for a watch; wounds are “closed right”.
    Omen: survival is possible, but costs effort.

  7. Salt-Veil
    Custom: thresholds salted; stores counted; water purified.
    Omen: protection holds, if maintained.

  8. Silence-Veil
    Custom: no music until the second bell; people speak softly.
    Omen: the sky listens.
